## Natural history notes

A small owlet moth characterized by mottled brown to grayish wings with darker patches, pale wavy lines, and a decorated bark-like pattern that helps it blend into tree trunks, dead leaves, and leaf litter. In Florida, it is found in hammocks, forests, pine flatwoods, forest edges, parks, and other wooded or semi-wooded habitats where suitable host plants and resting cover occur. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars feed on woody plant foliage and serve as part of the broader food web for birds, bats, spiders, wasps, and other insect-eating animals.
